items.title: Satellite pattern, companion, and winding number

references.title: Ryan Budney, JSJ-decompositions of knot and link complements in the 3-sphere
references.locator: §§1, 2, and 4; satellite patterns, companions, and companionship graphs

references.title: Allen Hatcher, Notes on Basic 3-Manifold Topology
references.locator: §1.2, torus decomposition conventions, printed pp.11–23

items.statement: Let $V=S^1\times D^2$ be the standard oriented solid torus, with oriented core $S^1\times\{0\}$. A **pattern** is a smooth oriented knot $P$ contained in the interior of $V$, together with a chosen closed tubular neighbourhood $N(P)$ contained in the interior of $V$. Its **winding number** $w(P)$ is the integer by which the homology class $[P]$ maps to $H_1(V;\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z$ under the isomorphism that sends the oriented core to $1$. The **pattern exterior** is $X_P=V\setminus\operatorname{int}N(P)$; its **outer torus** is $\partial V$ and its **inner torus** is $\partial N(P)$. A **companion** is a smooth oriented knot $K\subset S^3$ with a specified orientation-preserving tubular embedding $e:V\to S^3$ that sends the core to $K$ and identifies the solid-torus meridian and product longitude with the positive meridian and preferred longitude of $K$. The **satellite knot** $P(K)$ is $e(P)$, with chosen exterior $E_{P(K)}=S^3\setminus\operatorname{int}e(N(P))$; the image $e(\partial V)$ is its **companion torus**. The outer torus is **incompressible** when it bounds no properly embedded disk in $X_P$ with essential boundary on $\partial V$. It is **product-parallel** to the inner torus when $X_P$ is a product $T^2\times[0,1]$ with those tori as its ends. This definition alone asserts neither incompressibility nor essentiality of the companion torus.

items.title: Incompressibility, Seifert fibrations, and JSJ systems

references.title: Allen Hatcher, Notes on Basic 3-Manifold Topology
references.locator: §1.2, definitions preceding Theorem 1.9 and Lemma 1.10, printed pp.11–16

references.title: Walter Neumann and Gadde Swarup, Canonical decompositions of 3-manifolds
references.locator: §§1–4, canonical surfaces and torus-boundary JSJ conventions

items.statement: Let $M$ be a compact smooth $3$-manifold. A properly embedded surface is **two-sided** if it has a product neighbourhood $F\times[-1,1]$ in $M$. A **compressing disk** for a two-sided surface $F$ is an embedded disk $D\subset M$ with $\operatorname{int}(D)\cap F=\varnothing$ and $\partial D$ an essential simple closed curve in $F$; $F$ is **incompressible** if it has no compressing disk. A **boundary-compressing disk** is an embedded disk $D$ with $\partial D=\alpha\cup\beta$, where $\alpha=D\cap F$ is an arc not cutting off a disk in $F$, $\beta=D\cap\partial M$, and $\operatorname{int}(D)$ misses $F\cup\partial M$; $F$ is **boundary-incompressible** if it has no such disk. A surface is **boundary-parallel** if it cobounds a product with a subsurface of $\partial M$, and it is **essential** if it is incompressible, boundary-incompressible, and not boundary-parallel. $M$ is **irreducible** if every embedded $2$-sphere in its interior bounds an embedded $3$-ball in $M$. An incompressible torus is boundary-parallel if it cobounds a product $T^2\times[0,1]$ with a component of $\partial M$; $M$ is **atoroidal** if every incompressible torus is boundary-parallel. A **Seifert fibration** is a decomposition into circles with local models given by fibered solid tori; in the model $(D^2\times S^1)/\langle(z,w)\mapsto(e^{2\pi i/q}z,e^{2\pi ip/q}w)\rangle$, where $\gcd(p,q)=1$, the core fiber has multiplicity $q$. Fibers of multiplicity $1$ are **regular** and those of multiplicity greater than $1$ are **exceptional**. A finite family of pairwise disjoint incompressible tori is a **JSJ system** if every component obtained by cutting $M$ along the family is atoroidal or Seifert-fibered. It is **inclusion-minimal** if no proper subfamily is a JSJ system. Atoroidal does not mean hyperbolic.

items.title: Boundary-compressible annuli with torus boundary are boundary-parallel

items.statement: Let $M$ be a compact connected orientable irreducible $3$-manifold whose boundary components are tori. Let $A\subset M$ be a connected properly embedded incompressible annulus with $\partial A\subset\partial M$. If $A$ is boundary-compressible, then $A$ is boundary-parallel.
items.axiom_use: Choice-free. The ball is supplied by irreducibility; its marked windows and the finite smooth torus-curve reductions use explicitly choice-free suppliers.

items.title: Essential surfaces in a solid torus are meridian disks

references.title: Allen Hatcher, Notes on Basic 3-Manifold Topology

items.statement: Assume full AC. Let $V=S^1\times D^2$ be a solid torus. Every connected, two-sided, properly embedded incompressible and boundary-incompressible surface $F\subset V$ with nonempty boundary is a disk, either a meridian disk or a boundary-parallel disk. In particular, if $F$ is not boundary-parallel, it is a meridian disk. Any two smooth meridian disks with the same boundary admit a smooth isotopy of embeddings relative to that boundary, with a boundary-fixing topological ambient extension. If both disks are neat, this can be a smooth ambient isotopy relative to the boundary. In addition, every two-sided embedded torus $T\subset\operatorname{int}V$ has a compressing disk in $V$.
items.axiom_use: The original full AC hypothesis is retained and implies countable choice for the smooth general-position and Schoenflies suppliers. The smooth Loop criterion and new finite relative isotopy suppliers are choice-free. Full AC is also the explicit premise of the TOP cut-piece finite triangulation used in F10.

items.statement:
Assume countable choice. Let $M$ be a compact connected irreducible orientable smooth $3$-manifold with nonempty boundary, and fix a finite triangulation of $M$ with $t$ triangular faces. If $\mathcal T$ is any finite family of pairwise disjoint, two-sided, incompressible tori in $M$ such that no component obtained by cutting $M$ along $\mathcal T$ is homeomorphic to $T^2\times[0,1]$, then
$$
|\mathcal T|\le 4t+\dim_{\mathbb Z_2}H_2(M;\mathbb Z_2)-1.
$$
Consequently, any iterative process that cuts along tori and for which every finite stage satisfies this no-product condition terminates after finitely many cuts.
items.axiom_use: The finite-position and isotopy steps use countable choice through relative transversality; the finite combinatorial bound itself is choice-free.

items.statement: Let $B$ be either a pair of pants or a once-punctured Möbius band, and let $p:N\to B$ be a circle bundle whose total space is orientable. For each boundary torus $T$ of $N$, the inclusion $T\hookrightarrow N$ induces an injective homomorphism $\pi_1(T)\to\pi_1(N)$.

items.title: Every embedded torus in a ball is compressible

items.statement: Assume full AC. Let $B$ be a compact piecewise linear $3$-ball with a finite compatible triangulation, and let $T\subset\operatorname{int}B$ be a two-sided embedded torus, where two-sided means that $T$ has a product neighborhood with its given central inclusion. Then there is an embedded compressing disk $D\subset\operatorname{int}B$ with $D\cap T=\partial D$ and $\partial D$ essential on $T$. The disk is properly embedded in the closure of one component of $B\setminus T$: its boundary lies on that component's copy of $T$ and its interior lies in the interior of the component.
items.axiom_use: The original full AC hypothesis is retained and supplies both the proved TOP finite-triangulation bridge for the cut pieces and coset transversals in the amalgam argument. The disk transported back to the original ball is asserted TOP, without a silent PL or smooth marking upgrade.

items.statement: Assume full AC. Let $K$ be a nontrivial smooth knot with a specified companion solid torus $V=e(S^1\times D^2)$, let $P\subset\operatorname{int}(S^1\times D^2)$ be a pattern, and assume the outer torus of its pattern exterior $X_P$ has no compressing disk and is not product-parallel to the inner pattern torus. Let $T_c=\partial V=e(\partial(S^1\times D^2))\subset E_{P(K)}$ be the companion torus. Then $T_c$ is incompressible and is not boundary-parallel in $E_{P(K)}$; hence it is essential.

items.statement: Assume full AC. Let $M$ be a compact irreducible piecewise linear $3$-manifold with a finite compatible triangulation. Let $\mathcal T$ be a finite family of pairwise disjoint, two-sided, incompressible piecewise linear tori that are subcomplexes of that triangulation. Every component obtained by cutting $M$ along $\mathcal T$ is irreducible.
items.axiom_use: The original full AC hypothesis is retained. The repaired finite PL argument uses the choice-free explicit PL-ball compression supplier; it does not invoke a smooth triangulation theorem or an unqualified topological-torus supplier.

items.statement: Assume full AC. Let $K:S^1\to S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot with a chosen compact exterior $E_K$. There exists a finite inclusion-minimal collection $\mathcal T$ of pairwise disjoint incompressible tori in the interior of $E_K$ such that every component of $E_K$ cut along $\mathcal T$ is atoroidal or Seifert-fibered. Any two such inclusion-minimal collections are ambient isotopic in $E_K$. Atoroidal pieces in this statement are not asserted to be hyperbolic.

items.statement: Let $M$ be a compact connected orientable irreducible $3$-manifold whose boundary components are tori. Let $S\subset M$ be a connected, two-sided, properly embedded incompressible surface with nonempty boundary contained in $\partial M$. Then either $S$ is boundary-incompressible, or $S$ is an annulus boundary-parallel into $\partial M$.
items.axiom_use: Choice-free. The finite torus strips and the primitive marked-ball product supplier have choice-free proofs; no smooth global partition or triangulation supplier is used.

items.statement: Assume full AC. Let $M=E_{P(K)}$ be a satellite knot exterior with companion torus $T_c$. Suppose the pattern hypotheses of the essential-companion-torus lemma hold, both components of $M$ cut along $T_c$ are atoroidal or Seifert-fibered, and $M$ itself is neither atoroidal nor Seifert-fibered. Then the inclusion-minimal JSJ system of $M$ consists of a torus ambient isotopic to $T_c$. Cutting along that torus identifies the companion exterior $E_K$ as the component on the outside of the embedded companion solid torus. No conclusion is made for an essential companion torus that is absorbed into a Seifert-fibered union.

items.statement:
Assume full AC. Let $M$ be a compact connected irreducible Seifert-fibered $3$-manifold, and let $F\subset M$ be a connected, two-sided essential annulus or torus, neatly embedded at its boundary (the condition is vacuous for a torus). Then $F$ is ambient isotopic to either a vertical surface, meaning a union of regular fibers, or a horizontal surface, meaning a surface transverse to every fiber. For a horizontal surface $F$ with $n$ sheets over the base orbifold $B$ and exceptional-fiber multiplicities $q_1,\ldots,q_m$, the Euler characteristics satisfy
$$
\frac{\chi(F)}{n}=\chi(B)-\sum_{i=1}^m\left(1-\frac1{q_i}\right).
$$
If $F$ is two-sided and horizontal, cutting $M$ along $F$ gives an interval bundle over a surface.

For a smooth boundary-preimage embedding without the neatness condition, the same vertical-or-horizontal normal form is attained by a smooth isotopy of embeddings, fixed on the original boundary during its preliminary neatification, and by a topological ambient isotopy. The Euler count and interval-bundle conclusions apply to the resulting horizontal representative. A smooth ambient isotopy is asserted for the neat inputs above.
items.axiom_use: Full AC is retained from the original Statement and the solid-torus and simultaneous-system suppliers. It implies countable choice for smooth general position, flow and isotopy extension. No orientability hypothesis on M has been added.

items.title: Essential annuli in Seifert pieces can be made vertical

references.title: Allen Hatcher, Notes on Basic 3-Manifold Topology
references.locator: Lemma 1.14 and its proof, printed p.20

references.title: Walter Neumann and Gadde Swarup, Canonical decompositions of 3-manifolds

items.statement:
Assume full AC. Let $M$ be a compact connected orientable Seifert-fibered $3$-manifold and let $A\subset M$ be an incompressible, boundary-incompressible neatly embedded annulus. After an ambient isotopy and, if necessary, replacement by another Seifert fibration of $M$, $A$ is vertical. A change of fibration is needed only when the underlying manifold is $T^2\times I$ or the orientable twisted $I$-bundle over the Klein bottle. The twisted $I$-bundle over $T^2$ and $K\times I$ are nonorientable and do not occur under these hypotheses.

For an arbitrary smooth boundary-preimage annulus with the same disk-obstruction hypotheses, the conclusion holds by a smooth isotopy of embeddings with a topological ambient extension. The smooth ambient conclusion above requires neatness.
items.axiom_use: Full AC is inherited from the essential-surface classification supplier.

items.title: Boundary fiber slopes are unique outside the small Seifert exceptions

items.statement: Assume full AC. Let $M$ be a compact connected orientable Seifert-fibered $3$-manifold other than $T^2\times I$ and the orientable twisted $I$-bundle over the Klein bottle. Let $\mathcal A$ be a finite family of connected, two-sided essential annuli in $M$ such that every boundary torus of $M$ contains a boundary circle of some annulus in $\mathcal A$. Then any two Seifert fibrations of $M$ induce isotopic regular-fiber slopes on each boundary torus.
items.axiom_use: Full AC is inherited from the annulus-verticalization supplier.
